races.name: LSL Racing Horse Sales Syndication Leasing Handicap

runners_data.name: Ohara
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose recent form includes a win over 8f on soft, but today's 10f on good to firm is a clear step into new territory on both counts; Callum Hutchinson takes over and the pace scenario here leaves her needing a strong gallop that simply may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Capable on his day and won three runs back at a similar level; our figures rate him the pick of this field and he handles the going, though the step up to 12f for the first time is the one reservation today.

runners_data.name: Eloquencia
runners_data.note: In excellent form with three placings from four runs and a win over 10f on good — the trip and ground are exactly right — and Mason Paetel's 5lb claim is a genuine asset; her prominent style meshes perfectly with tracking the lone front-runner Battosai, making her the most naturally suited to how this race will unfold.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and progressive, she took a handicap at Ripon last time and arrived in good form beforehand; first-time cheekpieces add an angle for the step up to 12f, though she does carry a 4lb higher mark today.

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking is eye-catching for Andrew Balding's hold-up filly, whose best effort at 10f came on good ground, but her pattern of running from behind means she needs a stronger pace than Battosai alone is likely to generate; the hood is retained and she remains a danger if the race tempo opens up late.
runners_data.comment: Showed enough in placing third twice in recent starts to suggest some upside; first-time cheekpieces may sharpen his focus, and he handles this going, though a step up to 12f from proven form at 7f is a considerable shift.

runners_data.name: Battosai
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter who has shown consistent willingness to front-run over 10f on good ground across multiple outings; Jack Nicholls (5lb claim) inherits a free lead and his trainer's quiet 14-day strike rate is worth noting, though the horse's form figures of 0-5-2-4-5 suggest he finds it difficult to sustain the effort all the way to the line.
runners_data.comment: Placed runner-up three runs back but unable to build on it since; trainer is in good form and first-time cheekpieces add interest, though he is yet to score in recent starts and our figures put him at the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: Rumbustious
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's lightly-weighted prominent type drops into a much smaller field having run respectably in larger handicaps; Rob Hornby is an experienced handler of his style, and a record of consistent top-four finishes at 10-12f on good ground suggests he will not be far away if he can sit just off Battosai's pace.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts and ideally suited by today's trip and ground; fourth at Windsor last time was below his best but he looks attractively treated on a mark of 66, and our figures rate him among the main contenders despite his winless run.

races.paceDynamic: Battosai is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he can dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits Jack Nicholls. Eloquencia and Rumbustious are both prominent types who will look to sit just off the pace, meaning there is likely to be a small cluster in the early stages before the field strings out on the Chepstow straight. Ohara and Last Verse are hold-up horses who will be ridden patiently from the rear, setting up a straightforward sprint-for-home dynamic in the final two furlongs. On good to firm ground over 1m4f with a lone, uncontested leader controlling tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Battosai comfortably and pounce — pure hold-up horses face the additional burden of making up ground on a track and going combination that rewards those who are always travelling.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Battosai Leads, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai sets a controlled, sustainable gallop and a prominent tracker picks him off in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Battosai sets a controlled, sustainable gallop and a prominent tracker picks him off in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Battosai Completes Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai's controlled lead turns into a soft-gallop procession and no rival can close the gap from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Battosai's controlled lead turns into a soft-gallop procession and no rival can close the gap from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai and the prominent pair burn more fuel than expected in the middle stages and the hold-up horses find a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: If Battosai and the prominent pair burn more fuel than expected in the middle stages and the hold-up horses find a clear passage late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai is slow away or the pace collapses entirely, causing the field to bunch and race in a muddled fashion.
scenarios.body: If Battosai is slow away or the pace collapses entirely, causing the field to bunch and race in a muddled fashion.

watchPoints.text: Battosai is the only genuine pace-maker — if Jack Nicholls is forced wider than ideal at the start or loses his lead, the entire race shape collapses and the scenario probabilities shift dramatically.

Eloquencia's Mason Paetel is a conditional rider stepping up in responsibility with the 5lb claim; watch whether he settles her comfortably in second during the early stages rather than allowing her to overrace behind Battosai.

Last Verse has headgear (hood) retained after finishing eighth on her most recent start — if the hood is doing its job and Murphy gets a clean run from the rear, she represents the main danger to the prominent pair in the straight.

With only five runners on good to firm ground at Chepstow, the draw and early positioning will be settled very quickly; any horse that misses the break and finds itself trapped behind the small cluster early will face a long wait for daylight on the home straight.

races.name: UB40 Ft. Ali Campbell 24th July Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with two wins at 12f on similar ground (Stamford Bridge, good) and genuine front-running credentials; the visor is noted and Marcus Tregoning's stable is quiet of late (0/7 T14) but the track-trip-going alignment here is the tightest fit in the field, and with no rival likely to test her early, this is a structurally privileged position.
runners_data.comment: Showed good ability with back-to-back wins three and four runs ago and handles today's distance and ground well; first-time visor added after two successive below-par outings, and dropped 1lb she retains the profile to return to that level.

runners_data.name: Jindri
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a clear booking upgrade for Jane Chapple-Hyam and adds tactical nous from a hold-up position; Jindri's sole win came at Stamford Bridge over 12f in similar ground, but her recent form has been moderate (5th on last two starts) and the Chepstow track configuration — a long straight rather than the flat oval she favours — is an untested variable.
runners_data.comment: Promising filly who showed her ability with a win two outings back; form dipped at Kempton last time but she is unexposed at 12f and our figures suggest she has the capability to go well here.

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Ashley Lewis takes the 5lb claim and Grace Harris's yard has been in form (2/20 T14); Oasis Sunrise has won twice over 12f on good ground and finished placed in five of her last six starts at similar trips, giving her the most consistent form profile in the race and an ideal prominent style for a controlled-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last six starts and proven on this going; won a handicap at Leicester two outings back, though the most recent outing was a step back and the 12f distance takes her beyond her proven range.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: Laura Pearson rides a mare whose natural tendency is to race up with the pace, but in a field where Twilight Moon and Oasis Sunrise are ahead of her in the pecking order, she is likely to find herself racing slightly further back than ideal — David Loughnane's recent 3/21 T14 figures are encouraging, though Dance Time's form at this trip (3rd, 7th, 9th in recent 14f-16f runs) shows some inconsistency stepping up in trip.
runners_data.comment: Ran in better form last time when beaten just over a length at Carlisle, which offers some encouragement; however, her best efforts tend to come at distances beyond today's 12f, and she has ground to make up on the top-rated.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: George Wood partners a 6yo who has been absent for 104 days (72 days since jockey switch), and her form over marathon trips of 17f-19f at Goodwood represents a very different race style to this 1m4f test; that stamina-heavy profile and the extended layoff make her the most speculative runner in the field on pace-shape grounds.
runners_data.comment: Returning to the Flat after a hurdles outing, which makes her current form hard to gauge; trainer is in good form and she handles today's distance, but our figures put her at the foot of the field here.

runners_data.name: Nuptown Girl
runners_data.note: Harry Vigors (5) rides a mare who last won over 12f on good ground just seven days ago, giving her a strong recency edge; she is a genuine hold-up type by nature but the field configuration means she may need to race more forwardly than is ideal — Ian Williams's yard has been busy and productive (3/38 T14) and the weight of 118lbs is a clear asset at OR 58.
runners_data.comment: Bounced straight back here just seven days after landing a handicap at Newmarket, unchanged in the weights; proven at today's distance and on a sound surface, our figures rate her well clear of these rivals and she is the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Twilight Moon is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no horse likely to seriously dispute the lead, she can dictate her own rhythm from the gates on good-to-firm ground over this extended mile-and-a-half. Oasis Sunrise will press from a prominent position, but without genuine pressure from further back, Twilight Moon is likely to control the tempo at a sustainable rather than searching gallop, which compresses the race and reduces the advantage available to hold-up horses. Dance Time is a genuine prominent type but has been redistributed to midfield on the map because Twilight Moon and Oasis Sunrise are likely to occupy the front positions before she can establish her natural spot — the field carries more prominent profile than the pace topology can accommodate. This race shape strongly favours horses capable of racing close to a controlled pace and quickening from a handy position, meaning prominent-to-midfield types who can travel economically and produce a turn of foot in the straight hold the structural advantage over pure hold-up specialists.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Twilight Moon Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Twilight Moon dictates a comfortable fractions and the field fails to produce a decisive late surge, she converts front-running supremacy into victory.
scenarios.body: If Twilight Moon dictates a comfortable fractions and the field fails to produce a decisive late surge, she converts front-running supremacy into victory.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Oasis Sunrise tracks Twilight Moon efficiently and picks up sharply off a moderate tempo in the straight, she overhauled the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Oasis Sunrise tracks Twilight Moon efficiently and picks up sharply off a moderate tempo in the straight, she overhauled the leader inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and closers find a clear run through, a hold-up type catches the leaders in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and closers find a clear run through, a hold-up type catches the leaders in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Race Breaks Open
scenarios.trigger: If a challenger forces Twilight Moon to run a genuinely fast first half, the field strings out and an improver who handles a true gallop profits.
scenarios.body: If a challenger forces Twilight Moon to run a genuinely fast first half, the field strings out and an improver who handles a true gallop profits.

watchPoints.text: Twilight Moon and Oasis Sunrise: if Oasis Sunrise pushes for the lead at the start rather than settling second, she could inject an unexpected tempo that destabilises Twilight Moon's rhythm and reshapes the whole race.

Green Sky: a 104-day absence combined with a major trip drop (from 17f-19f to 1m4f) means her sectional behaviour in the first half-mile is genuinely unpredictable — monitor whether she settles or runs too freely from an unfamiliar position.

Nuptown Girl: despite winning seven days ago, her redistribution to midfield means she will likely race closer than her natural style demands; watch whether Harry Vigors attempts to push forward early and whether that disrupts the expected race order behind Twilight Moon.

Dance Time: if she fails to secure a prominent berth by the time the field rounds the home turn, the probability of a Scenario D disruption effectively falls to zero and Twilight Moon's control of the race becomes near-certain.

Going confirmation: the going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card heading saying Good — horses with proven good-to-firm form (Oasis Sunrise, Twilight Moon) receive a material upgrade over those whose form is primarily on easier ground.

races.name: togetheragainfestival.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamondonthehill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good recent course form over 7f on good ground, recording two placed efforts in similar conditions; wears hood, trained by Newland & Insole, and at 8 years old relies on getting a true pace to close into — a steady tempo led by Morte Point is not ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Placed three times in his last six starts but yet to win, and rated at the foot of our figures here; first-time cheekpieces arrive after a poor Salisbury effort last time, and his speed rating suggests ability remains untapped.

runners_data.name: Aspull
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground at Clive Cox's yard and boasts the best recent form in similar conditions (4/5 sim-going, 1W3P); 41 days since last run is a minor query but Cox horses often return fresh, and Jack Nicholls claims 5lbs making this a well-handicapped proposition if the pace suits.|
runners_data.comment: Showed his ability with solid efforts including a win before the current poor spell; he adds a first-time hood today and returns to conditions that suit at 7f on fast ground, making him a lively threat if finding that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Society Man
runners_data.note: Consistent poor run of form (504996) makes him hard to fancy regardless; a genuine hold-up type whose natural rear position is squeezed by other closers in this field, meaning he'll struggle to find his rhythm — six consecutive off-the-pace runs on this going have yielded zero wins or places.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent underperformer in his last six starts, and today's good to firm ground is against him given he does his best work with some cut in the going; hard to recommend despite a decent speed rating.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Comes back from 6f to 7f and is a true prominent racer who won over 6f on soft; Oisin Murphy takes the ride which is noteworthy, but six days since last run and a step up in trip means his natural front-end style may be curtailed by Morte Point's likely early lead — his best form has come at shorter.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a Salisbury handicap by a neck two outings back and ran to that level finishing runner-up last time; returns just six days later on the same mark with trainer in form and proven at today's distance and conditions.

runners_data.name: Dr Strangelove
runners_data.note: Top-rated alongside Morte Point at OR 86 and the standout prominent type in this race without a style conflict; Mason Paetel (5lb claim) is a plus on the weight, and three runs at 6-7f on good-ish ground show a horse who handles the conditions — is ideally drawn to sit second and produce a powerful sustained finish.|
runners_data.comment: Narrowly denied at Goodwood last time, going down by a nose off a 1lb lower mark; proven at today's 7f and conditions, with his recent form showing steady improvement, and our figures put him comfortably clear of this field.

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: Has shown he can front-run and win (1/7f/STA) but his recent Chepstow form is alarming — 12th and 21st in his last two runs on good ground at this course, and the [STYLE_FIT] flag tempers confidence in his chance of winning even as pace-setter; his role here is to set the race up, not necessarily win it.|
runners_data.comment: Proven at today's trip and on a sound surface, and shares the highest official rating in the race; recent form has been below par but he retains the ability to get involved if recovering his earlier level.

races.paceDynamic: Morte Point is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only five rivals in a six-horse field over 7f at Chepstow on good-to-firm ground, is highly likely to stride into an uncontested lead and control tempo entirely on his own terms. Dr Strangelove is the only other natural prominent type without a redistribution flag, meaning he will track Morte Point and keep the pace honest without necessarily applying real pressure. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Society Man is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot, and Supreme King is a true prominent type also displaced, meaning neither is likely to secure their optimal tactical position. With a single, uncontested pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop on a flat track, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or close from a genuine midfield berth and produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs — pure hold-up horses relying on a strong pace collapse to generate momentum are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Morte Point Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Morte Point crosses and leads without any serious early challenge and sets a controlled, even gallop.
scenarios.body: If Morte Point crosses and leads without any serious early challenge and sets a controlled, even gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Hotly
scenarios.trigger: If Supreme King pushes forward hard early and forces a genuine pace duel with Morte Point into the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Supreme King pushes forward hard early and forces a genuine pace duel with Morte Point into the first two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front pair tire rapidly through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front pair tire rapidly through the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Compresses Field
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys misjudge positions early and the race bunches at halfway, nullifying positional advantages.
scenarios.body: If jockeys misjudge positions early and the race bunches at halfway, nullifying positional advantages.

watchPoints.text: Morte Point's recent Chepstow form (12th, 21st on good ground) is a serious red flag — watch whether he holds a strong early position or falls away rapidly from the front once headed.|

Supreme King, a genuine prominent type, has Oisin Murphy aboard and may attempt to press Morte Point hard early; if he goes for it, watch for a pace spike in the first two furlongs that could dramatically change the shape.|
Aspull is 41 days off the track — watch his paddock behaviour and early running style; if Clive Cox has him cherry-ripe he has the best combination of proven going form and trip to close late.|

Society Man's redistribution means he is likely to find himself further forward than ideal; watch whether Mikey Sheehy attempts to sit off the pace anyway or is crowded into an unnatural position that costs him early momentum.|
Dr Strangelove carries top weight at 139lbs with a 5lb claimer — watch whether that weight concession to lower-rated rivals proves significant in the closing stages on good-to-firm ground over 7f.|

races.name: Fairplay Daily Price Boosts Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Flagraiser
runners_data.comment: Son of Flag Of Honour out of a dam who was useful over 5f at two; faces a tough ask on debut and rated last on our figures, though debut performances can always be deceptive.

runners_data.name: The Golden Snitch
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a promising debut but subsequent efforts have been disappointing; a return to that initial level is possible from this fresher mark, though the ground today is firmer than conditions he has shown his best form on.

runners_data.name: Vastern
runners_data.comment: Son of Wootton Bassett out of a dam who was useful at a mile; pedigree suggests he has every right to show up well on debut, though he remains unproven and our figures place him near the foot of the field.

runners_data.name: Fractional
runners_data.comment: Shaped well at Nottingham when runner-up last time, and returns in first-time hood with trainer in fine nick; rated well clear on our figures and gives the impression of a filly still well short of her ceiling.

runners_data.name: Name The Day
runners_data.comment: Showed enough on her first start to suggest genuine ability; form dipped at Southwell last time but she handles the going and the step to 7f could suit, with further improvement looking likely here.

runners_data.name: Deadline
runners_data.comment: Put in a below-par debut at Doncaster but entitled to step forward considerably with that experience behind him; he may also benefit from a different tactical approach here and holds solid claims on our figures.

runners_data.name: Far From Fern
runners_data.comment: By Far Above out of a dam who showed fair 6f form at two; entitled to learn from this debut outing, though others hold a more prominent place in the market here.

races.name: Bet Now With fairplaybet.co.uk Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Bama Lama
runners_data.note: Trainer Rod Millman sends out a mare returning on 18 days rest with a poor recent form string of 6476-6; a genuine hold-up type whose similar-going record reads 0 wins from 15 attempts, and being pushed into a midfield slot by weight of numbers makes her chance even harder to construct.
runners_data.comment: Form has been deteriorating over her last five starts, but she handles this course and distance well and acts on any going; the trainer is in form. A significant step forward is needed to feature here.

runners_data.name: Banana
runners_data.note: 246-day absence is the dominant flag here — Scott Dixon's seven-year-old has five AW runs in recent history and a solitary win, though that came over 5f at Southwell with a prominent run; returning to turf after such a layoff on fast ground with headgear (tongue-tie) adds further uncertainty to an already speculative profile.
runners_data.comment: After 246 days off the track, she returns in first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces; the Bath effort on softer ground was well short of her best, but this distance and surface suit her and she is the top-ranked runner on our figures.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard is in form (T14: 11/52) and this six-year-old has shown ability on Good going, but his true hold-up style means the prominent headgear (p) tag is potentially misleading — he will be squeezed by the race shape into a position he cannot exploit naturally, and his similar-going record of 0 wins from 15 is damning.
runners_data.comment: Placed a narrow third in a classified event at Brighton on his latest start, fitting cheekpieces today; handles this trip on good ground and all-weather, though his form has been patchy and he is yet to win.

runners_data.name: Darkened Edge
runners_data.note: The structural pivot of this entire race; Christopher Mason's trainer strike rate is excellent (T14: 3/7) and Darkened Edge's form on Good and similar going reads 1 win and 7 places from 10 attempts — the style fit as the lone pace-setter is near-perfect, and the STYLE_FIT tag here reflects only the redistribution context rather than any profound misalignment.
runners_data.comment: Handles 5f on fast ground and all-weather surfaces well, and her latest Bath handicap — a 3-length fourth — looks like a reappearance effort; she should come on for that run and is third on our figures.

runners_data.name: River Edge
runners_data.note: Three years off the track is an enormous question mark — this three-year-old ran exclusively on Good ground in its brief career and finished placed twice over 5f, but returning from 736 days away into a competitive 5f classified stakes demands a leap of faith that its hold-up style cannot easily justify.
runners_data.comment: Absent for over two years and back in a first-time hood; held and drifting right at Leicester on his latest outing, but he handles this distance and conditions — the hood may help if he settles, with fitness the key question after such a lengthy spell off.

runners_data.name: Snow Boots
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old carries a prominent ⚠ fade flag backed up by a winless and placeless recent record across turf; 45 days since last run and a form string of 8-5660 point uniformly in the wrong direction, and being redistributed into midfield from its natural hold-up position compounds an already weak profile.
runners_data.comment: Lowest-rated in the field, he has run over this distance before but is yet to show any consistent form; his latest outing at an extended trip at Lingfield was well below par, and a good deal more is needed here.

runners_data.name: Titus Thor
runners_data.note: Malcolm Saunders has only one runner in the 14-day window and this six-year-old's form of 070-95 alongside two consecutive fade flags leaves little to recommend — a true hold-up type pushed into midfield on a card that favours prominent racers, with zero wins or places on similar going from six attempts.
runners_data.comment: Tried at various distances in recent starts, he was beaten just over 3l in a handicap at Bath last time, broadly in line with expectations; handles this trip and going but has struggled for consistency and his speed figure gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris's three-year-old ran just two days ago — freshness is not the issue — and its form string of 262993 contains placed efforts on Good ground over distances from 5-6f; a genuine hold-up type by profile but one with the tactical flexibility to push closer if Daley T concedes the prominent ground, making it the most interesting closer in the field.
runners_data.comment: Well-experienced at 5f on a sound surface, he reappears two days after a disappointing Bath handicap and needs to rediscover his best; the quick turnaround is a factor, but he is second on our figures and clearly capable of better.

races.paceDynamic: Darkened Edge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Chepstow sprint on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rival likely to push her hard from the gates, she is set to control tempo from the off at a sustainable, self-dictated pace. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Bama Lama, Daley T, River Edge, Snow Boots, Titus Thor and Rogue Rebellion all want to come from off the pace — but with only one horse able to lead, the race shape is effectively handed to Darkened Edge to set. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate; of those, Daley T and Rogue Rebellion are the most likely to press forward and secure cover just off the lead, while the remainder will be forced wider or deeper than their natural position. A controlled, moderate gallop suits a prominent racer who can cross over and use the rail, and the sheer volume of hold-up horses forced to work through traffic on a tight 5f track tilts this race shape firmly in favour of those racing prominently or tracking the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Darkened Edge Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Darkened Edge breaks cleanly and sets a comfortable, uncontested lead with no rival willing to chase her down.
scenarios.body: If Darkened Edge breaks cleanly and sets a comfortable, uncontested lead with no rival willing to chase her down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a hold-up horse finds a clean passage to unleash a late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a hold-up horse finds a clean passage to unleash a late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Pressured Early
scenarios.trigger: If Daley T or another redistributed prominent type refuses to settle and pushes Darkened Edge into a faster-than-expected gallop.
scenarios.body: If Daley T or another redistributed prominent type refuses to settle and pushes Darkened Edge into a faster-than-expected gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems, slow breaks and multiple hold-up horses colliding for the same runs produce a scrambled finish with no clean result.
scenarios.body: If traffic problems, slow breaks and multiple hold-up horses colliding for the same runs produce a scrambled finish with no clean result.

watchPoints.text: Darkened Edge breaks cleanly — if she leads unchallenged from the gates the race is likely over early, watch the first two furlongs to see whether any rider commits to chasing her.

Rogue Rebellion ran just two days ago; watch paddock demeanour and early positioning — if Rob Hornby pushes forward rather than settling, the race shape shifts immediately and the pace dynamic changes.
River Edge's 736-day absence means a slow or anxious start is a real risk — George Wood will need to position quickly to avoid being buried in the pack of hold-up types competing for the same ground.

With six hold-up types in an eight-runner field, traffic congestion on the home bend at Chepstow is a strong possibility — any horse drawn wide without a clear run between the 2f and 1f markers is likely compromised regardless of ability.

Good to Firm ground (confirmed in going report despite race card stating Good) favours horses that can sustain early pace — any hold-up horse that fails to find a run inside the final furlong has no second chance on this surface or trip.

races.name: DragonBet Welsh Racing Festival 9th-11th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with recent course-relevant win over 8f on Good ground; Jason Watson partners a horse in excellent form (1-2 in last two starts) that handles this fast surface well and should set a sustainable lead from the off — STYLE_FIT tag signals she's racing in her natural role here.
runners_data.comment: Effective over this trip and going, she won by a short-head three starts back and has maintained her form since, finishing second off the same mark she carries today; she is our top-ranked runner, with the quick six-day turnaround the only flag.

runners_data.name: Violet Goldsmith
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up filly has one placing from five starts on similar going and hasn't won in her last five; Callum Hutchinson takes over and she'll need a strongly-run race to make her late effort count, which this pace dynamic may not fully deliver.
runners_data.comment: Moderate in her last several starts before a clear step forward when runner-up, beaten 5l in a handicap here on her latest outing; speedily bred for this sort of distance, she remains without a win but showed enough last time to merit respect.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence on a 3yo filly who has placed over 8f on Good ground twice and won over this trip is notable; runs from hold-up, but has enough tactical flexibility to arrive from midfield, and her recent form (4th, 1st, 3rd) suggests she's in decent shape.
runners_data.comment: Effective over today's distance and going and the winner on her penultimate start, she was held 3l back at Yarmouth last time — a minor blip that she is well placed to put right; she takes an eye-catching rider booking and is second on our figures.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with four placings and a win over 8f on Good or Good-to-Firm ground in her last five, making her the best-suited profile to sit just off Buckland Belle's pace and challenge in the straight; visor fitted, which sharpens focus, and Mason Paetel's 5lb claim is a live weight advantage on a horse with genuine each-way credentials.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who won narrowly off a lower mark in April and placed third last time at the same mark she carries today; she wears a visor for the first time on a quick four-day turnaround and handles this trip and going well.

runners_data.name: Paean Of Appin
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 3yo has a "fades in finish" flag, a trainer strike rate of 0/6 over 14 days, and only three career starts with modest returns; a true hold-up type whose mapped midfield position overstates his likely influence — this race shape does not set up kindly for him.
runners_data.comment: Lightly tried and yet to make the frame in recent starts, her latest effort showed marginal improvement at Windsor; bred to stay a mile and handles today's distance, with the trainer in decent form — but considerably more is needed to feature here.

runners_data.name: Very Demure
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a natural hold-up type placed to midfield on the map because of field congestion at the rear — Archie Watson's runner showed a second-place effort over 8f on Good ground in her history and has ability, but the redistribution means she won't be in her ideal position, constraining her finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Far from her best at Yarmouth on her latest outing, continuing a poor spell of form; she wears first-time blinkers and handles this trip and going, and has shown better on her day — but her trainer is out of form and much more is needed.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Unknown style with only three career runs, all modest placings, and a trainer (J S Moore) with 0/9 over 14 days; form reads 6-4-6 with no win or placing to recommend him, and the step to Good To Firm ground over 8f is uncharted territory — considerable uncertainty surrounds his role in the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Unable to get into contention when sixth in a maiden at Lingfield on his latest start, he handled the trip to place fourth the run before; improvement is required here, but he handles today's distance and is capable of better.

runners_data.name: Anorah Unleashed
runners_data.note: Unknown style tag, wears a tongue strap, and steps up from 6-7f to 8f for the first time in this race; three of her last five runs have been on faster ground and her best effort was a third over 6f on Good — the extra furlong is a question mark and her trainer has a modest 2/23 14-day strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time, she handles this distance and going well; beaten 3l at Carlisle last time off a slightly higher mark but a step forward is needed here, and the new headgear may provide a spur.

races.paceDynamic: Buckland Belle is the confirmed pace-setter on Good To Firm ground at Chepstow over one mile, and with no horse in this field both willing and able to pressure her early, she is set to control proceedings from the front at a measured, sustainable tempo. Alice's Influence is the one other prominent-style runner who could press closer to the pace, but the field contains significantly more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Paean Of Appin and Very Demure are genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield positions because they are unlikely to secure their natural slot in a compact eight-runner field, meaning their late-run threat is overstated by their mapped position. Ernie McCrew and Anorah Unleashed carry unknown style tags, adding a small unpredictability element, but neither has shown the profile to disrupt Buckland Belle's lead. With one horse controlling an uncontested, honest gallop on fast ground over a mile at Chepstow, this race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace, track the leader, and produce a sustained finish — patient chasers with genuine 1m form on good-to-firm ground are best positioned to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Buckland Belle — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs, the race may effectively be over early; watch whether Alice's Influence pushes up to apply any pressure or sits passive behind her.

Alice's Influence — fitted with a visor and racing just four days after her last run, monitor her early energy in the first furlong to confirm she is tracking up prominently rather than dropping back, as her whole race depends on maintaining a prominent position.

Very Demure and Paean Of Appin — both redistributed true hold-up horses mapped to midfield; if the pace is not strong enough to string the field, they risk getting caught in traffic in a compact eight-runner field and their finishing efforts may be blocked.

Ernie McCrew and Anorah Unleashed — two unknown-style runners whose early positioning is entirely unclear; if either decides to push forward and press Buckland Belle, the pace dynamic changes materially and the scenario probabilities shift toward hold-up horses benefiting.

Good To Firm ground confirmed for this race — all runners are tagged as OK for going, but Lady Of Clover's best form includes a win and multiple places on similar or softer surfaces, while Paean Of Appin's limited form base (3 runs) makes his true going preference genuinely unknown.

races.name: Family Fun Day 31st August Handicap

runners_data.name: Sanaam
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Crisford but recent form reads 7-1-9-8-4, showing only one win and patchy efforts; 15 days since last run is fine, similar-going record reads 4th and unplaced from two tries at 6f on Good, making this a tough ask from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Effective at today's distance on good-to-firm ground and all-weather, he tries first-time cheekpieces after showing a degree of encouragement at Southwell last time, beaten 2l off a slightly higher mark; an inconsistent recent record is the main reservation, though he is second on our figures.

runners_data.name: Star Material
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old who has been off 58 days — the freshness could sharpen or blunt; seven previous runs on similar going produced just one win from eight attempts, and the form string features two double-figure finishes, so consistency is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Boasts the strongest speed figure in the field and handles this trip on good ground; held at Chester last time off a higher mark than today's, and 58 days off the track — if he can put recent below-par runs behind him, a competitive mark could unlock better.

runners_data.name: Moscow Power
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who sets the entire pace map; won over this course and distance combination on Soft and has placed twice on Good ground at 6f, giving him solid credentials to dictate, though the STYLE_FIT flag signals he is operating here in his natural role and shouldn't be over-penalised.|
runners_data.comment: Effective at 6f on good-to-firm ground, he won over this trip and was performing well prior to a below-par York effort; his trainer's yard is in lean form currently, but on a fair mark he heads the rankings here.

runners_data.name: Evie Ross
runners_data.note: Recent form includes a win over 5f on Good and a fifth at this trip, and Clive Cox is in good order at 4/20 over the past fortnight; wears a blindfold (blinkers), which sharpen focus — though her natural inclination is to race from the rear, and in this field the prominent positions will already be taken before she gets competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Lowest on our figures, she carries a strong speed figure and has won in recent starts; held at Chester on her latest handicap outing, beaten over 4l, and the 6f trip may stretch her ideal distance range — first-time blinkers as connections seek improvement.

runners_data.name: Blue Orbit
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride, which is a significant booking upgrade; placed at 5f and 6f on Standard, with a fourth over this distance on Good, and has the tactical versatility to sit second or third before deploying a late challenge — well-suited to the likely race shape as a genuine prominent type.|
runners_data.comment: Effective at today's distance on a sound surface, he ran to his level at Southwell last time, beaten 2l off a slightly higher mark; takes a notable rider booking worth heeding, though a step forward is needed to feature at this level.

runners_data.name: Grey Horizon
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course and distance on Good just 10 days ago and wears a visor to sharpen concentration; back-to-back runs in quick succession can backfire but the recency edge is real, and Scott Dixon's yard is in steady form — his prominent racing style slots naturally into the pace map.|
runners_data.comment: Won by over a length at Brighton three starts back off a lower mark before a poor latest effort, seventh and beaten 6l off today's same mark; wears a visor for the first time and handles this distance and going.

runners_data.name: Double Naughty
runners_data.note: Has won once over 6f on Good ground and brings in solid placed efforts; Mason Paetel claims 5lb, reducing his burden to a workable level — but his natural style is closer-from-rear, and with the race unlikely to be run at a pace hot enough to bring true hold-up horses into it, he faces an uphill task.|
runners_data.comment: Won narrowly at Bath off a lower mark two starts back, with today's mark looking fair; however, her latest effort saw her beaten 10l off the same mark and she needs to find that form again — she handles this distance and going.

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 6f on Good and Soft are strong recent form credentials, and Rod Millman is quietly in form; however, her inclination to race from behind means she needs the pace to be genuinely fast — in a race where a lone front-runner is likely to control tempo, the gaps she requires may never truly materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Two successive wins to her name, including a comfortable success at Salisbury last time, with her trainer in good form; bred for speed at 5-6f and handles today's distance, though she takes on stronger opposition off a notably higher mark than on those recent wins.

races.paceDynamic: Moscow Power is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the gates at Chepstow's 6f. The Good to Firm conditions (confirmed by the going report despite the card listing Good) will reward an honest gallop rather than a sluggish one, meaning the pace should be genuine enough to test hold-up horses without being suicidal. Blue Orbit and Grey Horizon are the most likely to press from a prominent position and will track Moscow Power closely through the first two furlongs, shaping the mid-race pace into a controlled but not slack tempo. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Evie Ross, Double Naughty, and Maid In Devon are all genuine closers redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality all three will be switched off and running from the back; the prominent slots will be claimed by Blue Orbit and Grey Horizon rather than by the hold-up brigade. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a fair but unforced gallop — clearly favours horses who can race prominently or in a stalking mid-division position and produce a sustained finish, rather than pure closers who need a truly strong pace to generate the gaps they require.

watchPoints.text: Moscow Power jumps cleanly — if he doesn't establish the lead immediately, the entire pace map unravels and a scrappy race develops.|
